label: Parent-level purpose is already authored in two machine-readable carriers: the phase-parent template's PROBLEM & PURPOSE and goal.md's DURABLE DIRECTIVE Objective; the live corpus has 319 phase parents, 94 with goal.md and only 10 with acceptance-criteria.md.
No hop reads goal.md: 0 references in resume-ladder.ts, 0 across runtime/hooks and 0 in runtime/lib/continuity, so the durable directive is an authored purpose carrier with no reader.

Candidate (a) parent-level acceptance criteria fails the gap test and costs the most: the AC template has no purpose column, the phase level declares no optional addons, and enabling it touches the manifest, AC_CLOSURE scope, create.sh seeding and the template; only 10 of 319 parents carry the file.

Candidate (b) a parent-level user story or purpose section is a no-op: the phase-parent template already carries Problem & Purpose and the phase validator exempts parents, so adding the section changes no artifact and crosses no hop.
Candidate (c) an improved parent-specific template cannot close the gap alone because the parent template already carries the purpose; the missing piece is a reader.

Candidate (d) a purpose field in the continuity block is the most expensive: it needs the thin record and its MEMORY_0NN validation, the compact serializer, the save writer payload, the template and the resume parser, plus a fallback for 4657 existing implementation-summary.md files, and it leaves 29 handover-only packets uncovered.

Candidate (e) a purpose line in the compaction brief is feasible and cheap on Claude because lastSpecFolder is persisted in hook state, so one file read supplies the purpose, but it covers only the compaction hop and needs per-runtime wiring.

Recommendation: candidate (f) one purpose row on the resume surface is the smallest change that closes the measured gap — add purpose to ResumeSignal, extract '### Purpose' from the spec-doc snapshot already read, and render a Purpose row in the RESUME BRIEF; two files and one test, no schema change, no migration, no new authoring.

Candidate (f) has the widest coverage per unit of effort because every runtime's recovery pointer already lands on /speckit:resume (claude session-prime, dsh, devin, pi), so one read-side addition reaches every hop the operator described.

Validation plan for the recommendation: fixture tests in resume-ladder.vitest.ts for a filled spec.md purpose, a goal.md-only carrier and a no-purpose packet, plus one manual /speckit:resume against this packet checking the rendered row.
